essence: The supreme secret of cakra-arising is introduced.
The effortless form is named; the effort-born is seed-syllable-natured, of consciousness-vibration.
Leading supreme consciousness resembles buckets on a water-wheel.
One-pointed effort wins the wondrous wheel-rise; concentrated force gives mantra-rise by night.
The mantra-deity pleases through efforted identity; sky-taste, one-eye, eternal-rise, half in twin seeds.
The rise holds three thousand seven hundred; four yields five thousand four hundred.
Five syllables give three thousand three hundred twenty; six gives three thousand six hundred.
Seven gives three thousand six hundred eighty; eight varies by twenty-seven hundreds.
Nine syllables yield twenty-four hundreds; ten yields twelve hundred sixty-one.
Śiva-syllable gives one thousand nine hundred sixty-four; twelve gives eighteen hundreds.
Thirteen gives sixteen hundred sixty-two; bhuvana-syllable gives fifteen hundred forty-three.
Fifteen gives fourteen hundred; sixteen gives thirteen hundred fifty.
Seventeen gives twelve hundred seventy; eighteen gives twelve hundred to the wise.
The twenty-four cakra gives nine hundreds; the twenty-seven gives eight hundreds.
The great thirty-two cakra gives six hundred seventy-five; the doubled twenty-four gives a hundred four and a half.
The lump-yoga knower marks rise in lump-mantras; the fifty-four cakra gives four hundreds.
Thirty-seven and a half gives three hundred eighty-eight; the three-part gives two hundred sixty-six.
The eighty-one cakra's rise follows the breath; the ninety-six cakra gives two hundred and a quarter.
The hundred-eight cakra yields two hundreds; this cakra is six times doubled.
Then doubled, eighth-part, half, middle, half, one — then subtle halves by skill.
A sixteenth-part subtle motion is marked; so the yogin whose breath is effort-restrained.
Swallowing marks breath-order; time-contraction follows the swallowing.
Consciousness is one and full once knowledge-difference is removed; breath rising ceases to be new.
Without time-difference, knowledge-difference does not arise; object-difference no more than a ring of mountains.
Time is its divider, a subtle instant; the subtlety's limit holds as long as the moment.
Otherwise even the skilled cannot express it; knowledge would not shine without it.
Its absence, as long as present in the eye-path, marks union or separation in object or self.
If vibration arises, that is surely breath; without breath-vibration it would not be.
Its absence is not knowledge-absence; intellect is not that, being far from time-difference.
Time must touch consciousness; so one consciousness takes many forms.
Knowing without thought still thinks in the object-domain; while no other vibration rises, he remains one.
So long as one thought conjures varied objects; who not knowing them has no thought arise.
He would not be anyone in three worlds; thought is called knowledge by word-attachment.
She too would be sequential; what to think, how, who? Even a pot would need thought.
Not-thought belongs to one abiding in measure and non-measure; knowledge-collection fails from non-simultaneity.
Thus this transaction is thought-born; while other-vibration does not rise, he is one.
Knowledge touches thought's apex; the eighty-one cakra's great power is reflection-natured.
Thought bestowing Śiva-state is told as 'I make the ears dance'.
From cakra-motion effort, the cakra is intellect; japa, homa, worship follow from breath-equality.
Siddha doctrine names Kuṇḍalinī as breath-equal-transcendent; Yoginī-Kaula too, by the Lord.
Word-mantra-syllable follows cakra-division; the mantra-knower then bears fruit in japa and the rest.
Two-, three-, seven-, eight-numbered omit śakti-rise; such are śakti-abiding, vidyā, or cakra-leaders.
Knowing one's word-lump's form, joined always: eternal-rise, great-principle, rise-abiding, Sadāśiva.
Unjoined to śakti-path and unrecited by rise, they never succeed though recited by millions.
In garland-mantras all is mental recitation; whispered śakti-rise should not be arranged.
In word-mantras recite as far as word-śakti reaches, constantly joined, by sādhakas.
Their number is the word called 'word'; having made the rise, begin from the three-word statement.
In the twelve cakra, twelve-named gives a hundred and a half; the rise gives four hundred forty.
The sixteen cakra in twelve gives two hundred ninety-four; equal half yields a hundred twelve.
The sixteen-named within sixteen gives eighty-four; the rise gives two hundred fifty-six.
Four eight-parts, three excess the wise say; in eight-eight, quarter-half twenty vasus.
The rise is seven hundred sixty; this cakra-rise benefits sādhakas.
Resting mental fluctuations in the cakra, resting as long as risen — that is the motion-rise.
In the full, three: entry, identity, exit; the middle rise is best for accomplishment.
Free of first and last rise, the middle rise shares accomplishment with mantra, vidyā, cakra.
The mantra-cakra-rise knower and vidyā-cakra-rise knower accomplish quickly, as taught in twenty-three.
Two, three, four syllables: vidyā or cakra; recite always separate from principle-rise.
One by one via lump-syllable-word, śakti-principle-going; many-syllabled is mantra, vidyā, or cakra.
Śakti-abiding is not there; division is oṃ-ending; therefore rise three-by-three day and night.
The division divides three-by-three again; rest in the first rise, rise by the second.
Enter half-half union; half-rise gives the full-rise self in equal three-part time.
Entry, rest, rise — the own-third rise; thus time-abundance rests in breath.
He in place, in sky, in that consciousness; thereby this universe abides; consciousness-establishment pairs with dissolution-rise.
At śakti's end-sound, vibration countless and real; as the Mālinī says, in the body anywhere.
Modification arises, that principle supreme; breath establishes time, then absorbed in whatever body.
In this body's body, form is determined; the last grossness of consciousness-vibration-breath is suṣumnā.
She becomes nāḍī-form and spreads the body; Svacchanda likens it to a leaf's threads.
The body is pervaded by door-water-nature through nāḍīs, from big toe to Brahmakuṇḍalinī's end.
All time spans eighty-four finger-widths; subtle time abides up to twelve.
Ninety-six below-six, twofold, hundred-eight hundreds; the breath-rise-dissolution interval moves in the middle.
Universe creation-dissolution from wind-order; this subtle-reflection cakra-rise is spoken by experience and scripture.

rasa.dominant: adbhuta (wonder) with śānta weight (the rise of cakra cycles in the breath; rest in the sealed consciousness)
rasa.justification: The ahnika teaches the rise of cakra cycles in the breath: effort-born concentration swallows time and unifies consciousness; wonder at the cycle crowns the practice.

sections.SUMMARY: The ahnika teaches the cakrodaya: the rise of mantra cycles in the breath, from effortless to effort-born, through numerical rises, time and knowledge, japa rules, and the body as field of time.
sections.FUNCTION: Establishes cakrodaya: the rise of mantra cycles in the breath — effort-born concentration swallows time, unifies consciousness, and the body becomes the field of time.
sections.KEY TERMS: cakrodaya (rise of cakras), prāṇacāra (breath movement), grāsa (swallowing), saṃvitti (consciousness), kṣaṇa (moment), vikalpa (thought), mantra, vidyā, japa, śakti, prāṇa, nāḍī, suṣumnā, Brahmakuṇḍalinī, Mālinī-tantra, Svacchanda
